items.title: Jensen Huang says he would come back as Nvidia's CEO if America needs him – a technique I now intend to use at my next job interview
items.summary:
Jensen Huang says he would be honoured to return to his role as Nvidia's CEO should the company's board want him. The problem for Huang is, the board don't seem to. 

In a statement sent to CNN , among others, Huang lays out his now clear-as-day faults and makes a pitch for his old job back.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang says.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

President Donald Trump and a cohort of silicon valley execs have previously backed the Nvidia co-founder, even if Trump did wobble his way over to backing ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for a day. A heap of signatures were also added to a #bringjensenback petition , supposedly including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Sweeney has barely come up for air he's so wound up about Huang's resignation. 

Yet all these big names won't mean much if Huang can't convince the company's board of directors.

Last we heard, Nvidia's board was intent on moving past Huang . That's according to someone close to the matter speaking to CNBC . There are also a lot of things hanging over Huang at the moment, including an internal investigation at Nvidia, a couple of chats with Congress , an ongoing investigation into Nvidia's customer, Megaspeed , and any potential share price shock as markets would react to the news.

items.title: 'I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM' says Sam Altman, weeks after seeming to say the opposite
items.summary:
Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor , he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge ).

Altman says, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great."

So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". He argues that the optimal way to use memory is to share it (in this case, he seems to be referring to the use of AI in home rigs), and "have it working 100% of the time. Rather than, like, sometimes off in someone's Edge device."

So I guess if we all share RAM, we get more at the end of the day. I'll wait for OpenAI to share its memory with me, and then I might do the same. 

Altman points out that he got in more trouble a few years ago for saying there would be "a huge squeeze on memory". He then notes that many didn't believe it would be such a worry, and "we have seen DRAM prices, I don't know exactly, but maybe they went up like 5x, 7x or something like that. I think it would be much better if the world just had a lot of memory."

(Image credit: Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg via Getty Images) AI sever demand…

items.title: TCL CSOT's new OLED panels might not only be cheaper, but also have high refresh rates and hassle-free pixel burn-in compensation
items.summary:
I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now. It might just be the company that brings OLED monitor prices down thanks to its use of the inkjet-printing (IJP) process in manufacturing. TCL CSOT had already said it was moving in equipment for IJP manufacturing and expected production in the fourth quarter of 2027, but the company is now showing off some pretty impressive panels made using the process.

According to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp ), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech. Apparently, the company describes this monitor as having the "world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation system."

You already knew what that was, right? No, me either. According to Display Specification's understanding of the announcement, it's tech that "continuously adjusts image performance in the background without requiring periodic compensation cycles while the display is powered off."

OLED pixels can degrade at different rates, which is what causes pixel burn-in. The usual method for solving this is to run compensation cycles while the display is off, which takes a few minutes and boosts underperforming pixels up a bit back to where they should be. 

It sounds like TCL's new tech will somehow allow this to happen without turning the monitor off, and will just happen as it's being used. Which might compensate for pixel burn-in without as much hassle. Just bear in mind that the word here is "compensation", not…
items.t: TCL CSOT's new OLED panels might not only be cheaper, but also have high refresh rates and hassle-free pixel burn-in compensation

items.title: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year
items.summary:
AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp ), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors. If that sounds like gibberish to you, effectively, this lays the groundwork to more efficiently handle AMD chips that have different core types. 

Up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength. AMD's current heterogeneous design pairs full-fat Zen 5 and lower-caste Zen 5C cores together in Zen 5 chips nowadays, but there is far less actual difference between these two core types than in the P-cores and E-cores of modern Intel architectures. 

But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different. Also shared in a Linux patch earlier this year , Zen 6 is set to introduce a new Low Power core type (which is set to run at a very low power, as you might guess from the name), and that is a core type that would really benefit from Capacity Aware Scheduling. 

What AMD has called Performance and Efficiency cores up until now is not the same as what Intel has called Performance and Efficiency cores. AMD's Efficiency cores are effectively just compact versions of the Performance cores, whereas Intel's E and P cores have different microarchitectures and are specifically tailored for different use cases. 

The new Zen 6 LP cores appear to be similar to Intel's LPE (Low Power Efficiency) cores you will find in its Panther Lake chips . And as such, the need for CAS makes more sense. If AMD LP…
items.t: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year

items.title: Elsinore Review
items.summary:
Elsinore is in theaters on Nov. 20. 

Another award season, another Shakespeare-adjacent film starring a well-liked actor who is apparently overdue for their state mandated awards campaign. Yes, since Jessie Buckley soared straight to an Oscar win last year for playing the Bard’s long-suffering wife Agnes in Chloé Zhao’s pretty good historical drama Hamnet, apparently it’s now time for another thespian to make a claim for the throne. This time it’s the ever-reliable Andrew Scott — an actor I’m never mad to see pop up in anything — working with director Simon Stone, who I’ve never had a strong opinion about one way or the other. The Swiss-born Australian filmmaker claims a profound love for Shakespeare’s works, so it makes sense for him to jump at the chance to direct a movie about a man who would do anything to make his mark playing Hamlet before he dies. If only such passion had also managed to conjure up a good reason for the film to exist.

Elsinore, named for the castle where the events of the play Hamlet take place, stars Scott as Scottish actor Ian Charleson, an actor most famous for his work in 1981's Chariots of Fire and for later succumbing to AIDS after his National Theatre run as Hamlet in late 1989. items.title: Nvidia tightens up control of its own national security policies as it cozies up to US government with new board-controlled committee
items.summary:
I've already had to write the word 'committee' a lot in recent weeks, due to the scandal developing over at Nvidia leading to CEO Jensen Huang's resignation . He's off to see a couple of committees in Congress in coming weeks. Though today it's Nvidia's turn to establish a committee: the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, or NSECOC as I will hereafter call it.

The NSECOC will answer direct to the Nvidia board. It's also led by a board member, Suzanne Nora Johnson, former vice chairman of Goldman Sachs Group. Though the company says it will keep independent experts around for advice and expertise. It will work with the existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team at Nvidia, which will now report to the committee and interim CEO, Colette Kress.

It looks to me like the company's board want to know who Nvidia is sending its GPUs to at all times; something that will be of utmost import in coming months and years as the company's customers have come under recent scrutiny by US lawmakers and agencies. An investigation is being carried out by the US Department of Justice into one of its customers, Megaspeed, the agency confirmed yesterday .

It also means the board has a say in the question of who gets Nvidia's GPUs while the company looks for a new CEO. As it stands, the company's CFO Kress is in the big chair at Nvidia HQ, but the company is looking for a replacement. items.title: Nintendo Suffers Rare Review Bombing For Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy
items.summary:
Nintendo fans are hitting the company with a rare review bombing campaign, to register their dissatisfaction with Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy .

The Switch 2 upgrade for Nintendo's brilliant Pikmin 4 launched last week as a paid add-on, priced $9.99. It adds a fresh challenge mode, Dandori Academy, and bumps up the overall package's visuals to 4K.

Each month, six new challenge levels will be available to practice, with the ability to file competitive times during a limited time window each weekend. That’s because many of these emulators and tools were AI-assisted, which is also why you have seen so many other “native” PC ports of games floating around (to mixed results — and fears concerning how safe they actually are to play).

Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.
items.t: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Look, I'll be real with you. When I installed Drag Meets – Quick n Dirty Edition , I was not expecting it to go well. Cars spend most of their time flying and exploding in my copy of Grand Theft Auto 5, and these circumstances aren't conducive to gentlemanly racing.

I didn't anticipate it going quite as badly as it did, though. Drag Meets is actually rather complex: you don't just rock up to an objective marker, tap E, and get warped behind the wheel of a car. There's a lite social sim element to the whole thing, so you walk up to an objective marker, tap E, and suddenly find yourself standing in the midst of a drag racing soirée .

Drag meets are a scene, it turns out, and the scene's members have names, goals, and ambitions. A racer named "Blue Anime Panto" is seeking a challenger, the notifications inform me. "Blade had joined the meet", reads another. A lady called Tempesta has been forced to leave the meet because her engine broke, apparently. How did this happen? Either it's a randomly rolled event or her car flew into the sun; I am unable to tell.

It's not just Tempesta who's leaving the meet. Everyone is leaving, on account of the airborne minivan, just overhead, filled with hitmen determined to kill us all. They should be determined to kill me and only me, but Lamar (from GTA 5, you know? Lamar was also there.…

items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

"The idea of letting players freely choose a starting point for their adventure has been discussed, with the goal being to offer players a range of choices, rather than prescribe their experience according to my philosophy," Yoshida wrote.

items.title: We almost got a medieval Call of Duty with knights and swords: 'If it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty'
items.summary:
Call of Duty is an inherently conservative series. You know what you're getting: guns, explosions, cinematic flourishes inspired by action movies, and probably some jingoism. And that's largely what the annual series' adherents seem to want. But it could be so much more. 

Taylor Kurosaki, writer and co-director for Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare , tells us he still thinks it has broad potential. That's why Infinite Warfare was set in the future—though, at the time, the team didn't realise it would end up being the third futuristic CoD, following Advanced Warfare and Black Ops 3. 

"Look, Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right? It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

I would love for that to be true. Call of Duty: The American Revolutionary War, Call of Duty: The Hundred Years War, Call of Duty: Napoleon. A military romp that isn't set between 1941 and 2065. After 23 years, it would be nice to see it spread out a bit. 

But big swings are not in CoD's nature. Or rather, Activision isn't particularly interested in rocking the money boat. A medieval CoD isn't the only massive detour the series almost took. Before it was forced to salvage Infinity Ward's Modern Warfare 3, Sledgehammer was working on a third-person horror game set in Vietnam, called Call of Duty: Fog of War .

items.title: Biostar announces the first Intel Panther Lake motherboard and it's tiny, but don't get your hopes up for cramming it into a mini gaming PC
items.summary:
Motherboard manufacturer Biostar has just announced the BIPTL-IHT, a mini motherboard complete with an integrated Panther Lake-H processor. It's the first desktop Panther Lake motherboard to be released in retail.

As spotted by VideoCardz , the motherboard range has support for up to 128 GB of DDR-7200 MHz SO-DIMM memory and can come with the following chips:

Intel Core Ultra 5 325 / 335 / 336H Intel Core Ultra 7 355 / 365/ 356H / 366H Intel Core Ultra 9 386H All of these chips come with Xe3 graphics with four Xe cores, and are lacking the punchy integrated B390 iGPU (and its 12 Xe3 cores) that some mobile Panther Lake chips have. You can still do some light gaming on these integrated graphics, but you won't be making yourself a mini gaming PC with Biostar's latest. 

Instead, it seems like the purpose of this motherboard is to support industrial PCs, but given Xe3 graphics support hardware-accelerated AV1 encoding and decoding, one could feasibly use the motherboard in a mini media server PC instead. 

You are getting two M.2 Key-M slots here, with PCIe 5.0 x4 and PCIe 4.0 x2 connections. This allows for NVMe storage, and the memory is dual-channel too. You also get two HDMI ports, two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, and the motherboard can support up to four displays at once. 

As it's a 'Thin' Mini-ITX motherboard, its dimensions are 170 mm by 170 mm. That's very small. We don't yet have a release date or price point for this motherboard range. 

Still, it's a bit of a shame we don't have any mini motherboards with gaming-worthy integrated Panther Lake mobile chips yet.…
items.t: Biostar announces the first Intel Panther Lake motherboard and it's tiny, but don't get your hopes up for cramming it into a mini gaming PC

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough

Final Fantasy 14 is set to make some big changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and new raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.

And judging by a recent Letter from the Producer , Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed."

I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. items.title: The Sunday Papers

Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator.
